A3_retry_identity_F3.finding: ingest/ingester.py aligns request messages to the ingested history by content only. A request whose message keys equal the previous confirmed request is treated as a retry (request events suppressed), and a longest-common-run alignment can cover the whole request when content repeats, so the newest user message is dropped while completeness stays 'complete'. Reproduced at 0801866 before this amendment: a host that sends 'yes' every call and keeps a 4-message window gives 3 user events for 10 calls; a host alternating 'yes'/'no' with a 4-message window gives 4 user events for 12 calls (window 6: 4 and 5; window 8: 6 for alternating). The drop is therefore wider than the retry branch.
A3_retry_identity_F3.signals_examined: request id: a fresh uuid per call, so it cannot link a retry to its original. Positions: the window slides, so a position is not stable across calls. Message identity: the tap sees only content (hosts copy message objects, so object identity is not reliable). Response linkage: sound only on the assumption that the host kept the previous response in its window. Delivery state: the tap knows only that it handed a response to its caller, not that the host used it. No signal in the stub tap distinguishes a retry or regeneration from a legitimate repeat. The limit is stated, not hidden.
A3_retry_identity_F3.design: (1) Fail-safe: without a host-declared retry the final message of a request is never suppressed. If content alignment would leave no new message, the last message is emitted as a new occurrence with meta ambiguous_repeat=true, a non-blocking gap 'ambiguous_alignment' is opened, and completeness() reports it in a new field ambiguous_calls. The same gap opens when the maximal alignment is not unique (tie among equal-length runs). A true undeclared retry therefore yields a flagged possible duplicate, never a loss. (2) Explicit retry identity: tap.call(request, stream=False, retry_of=None) records a host-declared retry_of (the call number being resent) in the REQ body. The ingester honours it only when it names the immediately preceding confirmed call and the message keys are identical; the suppression is made visible as a port event 'declared_retry'; a claim that does not meet that test is ignored and recorded as a port event 'retry_claim_ignored'. ASSUMPTION: a host that declares a retry is honest; nothing here can verify it.
A3_retry_identity_F3.tests: ingest/tests/test_delta.py. Each fails on 0801866 code and passes after the fix: same-text window 4 and 6 (all yes) and alternating yes/no windows 4, 6, 8 give one user event per call, both providers; two consecutive identical turns yes, yes both ingested; an undeclared identical resend yields a flagged duplicate and ambiguous_calls; a declared retry yields one request event and a declared_retry port event; a false retry claim is ignored; the existing unique-text windows (items 7 and 11) show no ambiguity flag.
A3_retry_identity_F3.new_item_13_repeated_content_hosts: patterns {all 'yes'; alternating 'yes'/'no'; cycle 'a','b','c'} x windows {4, 6, 8 messages, trimmed from the front after each exchange} x providers {anthropic, openai}, 20 calls each, stub answer 'ok' every call = 18 runs. Pass: in 18/18 runs user events == 20 and assistant events == 20 and the multiset of (call, side, provenance, kind, text) equals the independent oracle of A4; zero blocking gaps. Reported, no floor: how many runs carry an ambiguous_alignment gap. Control for the oracle comparison: unique-text hosts (q0..q19, windows 4 and 8, both providers = 4 runs) must carry zero ambiguity flags (a flag there is a false positive; floor 0 of 4).
A3_retry_identity_F3.new_item_13b_retry_probe: per provider and 10 seeds: (a) undeclared identical resend after a returned response: 2 user events, the second flagged ambiguous_repeat, ambiguous_calls lists the call, 10/10; (b) declared retry: 1 user event, 2 assistant events, a declared_retry port event, no ambiguity flag, 10/10; (c) retry_of naming a call whose keys differ: claim ignored, retry_claim_ignored port event and the request events present, 10/10.
A3_retry_identity_F3.claim_change: The claim 'exactly once' becomes 'every message the host sent is ingested at least once; an identical resend that is not declared by the host is ingested as a flagged possible duplicate'. tests/test_ingest.py test_identical_resend_is_marked_retry pinned the old behaviour and is changed in the same commit as the fix, with this note.

A4_independent_oracle_F4.finding: items 2a/2b/2c/2d compared the arm only with a baseline made by the same Ingester, so an omission shared by both passes.
A4_independent_oracle_F4.oracle: ingest.proofs_common expected_events_of_conversation: the expected multiset of (call_n, side, prov, kind, ident) is built at the host while the scripted conversation runs, from the messages the host appends and the response object the stub returns. It imports no Ingester, reads no log record and no event key. ident is the text for text blocks, the thinking text for thinking blocks, the tool id for tool calls and tool results. The tuples are re-derived from provider message structure by a small function in proofs_common (not shapes.blocks_of_message).
A4_independent_oracle_F4.applied_to: item2a (20 seeds x 2 providers), item2b (10 x 2), item2c (5 x 2), item2d (10 x 2), item 13 (18 runs) and the crash matrix already has its own table. Every row records oracle_match; the baseline comparison is kept.
A4_independent_oracle_F4.pass: oracle_match true in every run of those items (20/20, 10/10, 5/5, 10/10 per provider; 18/18).
A4_independent_oracle_F4.control: SharedOmissionIngester (controls.py): an Ingester that never writes events of kind 'thinking', used for both the baseline and the arm of the item2a delivery shape on 20 seeds (anthropic; seeds with a thinking turn). Floor: arm equals baseline in >=18/20 runs (the old comparison cannot see it) AND oracle_match is false in >=18/20 runs (the new oracle does). Reported as item2f.

A5_claim_wording_F5.deviation_item4: PREREG.json item4_provenance registered n = 40 conversations per placement, with thresholds expressed over 40 (marker strings 0 of 40, quote-back flagged 40/40, forged block stays user 40/40). The implementation (proof_items_456.py item4, SEEDS[:7]) ran 7 conversations per placement: 7 placements x 7 = 49 conversations, of which 6 placements x 7 = 42 are covered placements and 7 are the host_alters_block placement, which fails by design and is reported separately. This was not documented in amend-1 or amend-2 and was a sample-size deviation from the registration. No 40-per-placement run exists. The registered thresholds at n=40 are therefore NOT met or claimed; what is measured is 7/7 per placement. This amendment records the deviation; it does not rerun item 4 at n=40.
A5_claim_wording_F5.wording_rule: Every sentence in ingest/CLAIMS.md carries its own denominator and names what it does not cover. The crash claim reads 'named-hook matrix' not 'any point'. The provenance claim separates six covered placements from the failing altered-block placement. The re-scored scanner figure is described as a positive-only recall figure on an equally weighted synthetic set under a stated predicate.
